overview: SPREAD introduces a diffusion-based generative framework for multi-objective optimization that trains a conditional DDPM with shifted objective conditioning to guarantee dominance improvement, and refines candidate solutions during reverse sampling via MGD-inspired adaptive guidance and Gaussian RBF repulsion for diversity, evaluated across online, offline, and Bayesian MOO settings.

modules.name: Decision Space Sampling and Dataset Construction
modules.description: Implements Latin hypercube sampling (LHS) over the decision space to generate training data points, computes their objective values, and constructs the shifted conditioning labels C = F(X) + Ξ with strictly positive shift vectors for conditional DDPM training.

modules.name: DiT-MOO Architecture
modules.description: Implements the Diffusion Transformer adapted for multi-objective optimization, including input projection, timestep embedding, objective-value conditioning via multi-head cross-attention (MHCA), layer normalization, and output projection for noise prediction conditioned on objective values and diffusion timestep.

modules.name: Cosine Variance Schedule
modules.description: Implements the cosine variance schedule for the forward diffusion process, computing cumulative noise-retention coefficients ᾱ_t and per-step variances β_t using the shifted cosine parameterization to allocate more steps to low-noise regions.

modules.name: Conditional DDPM Training Loop
modules.description: Implements the full training loop for the conditional DDPM, including forward diffusion noise injection at random timesteps, shifted-condition label construction, MSE loss computation between true and predicted noise, early stopping logic, and gradient-based parameter updates.

modules.name: Multiple Gradient Descent (MGD) Direction Computation
modules.description: Implements the MGD sub-problem solver that finds optimal convex combination weights λ* on the standard simplex minimizing the norm of the weighted gradient sum, yielding the common descent direction g(x) = Σ λ*_j ∇f_j(x) for each candidate point.

modules.name: Gaussian RBF Repulsion for Diversity
modules.description: Implements the Gaussian RBF-based repulsion function Γ_t(Y_t) over pairwise objective-space distances with adaptive length-scale σ, computing the repulsion penalty that discourages clustering and promotes spread along the Pareto front.

modules.name: Main Direction Optimization Sub-Problem Solver
modules.description: Implements the optimization sub-problem (Eq. 13) that balances MGD alignment (maximizing inner product with MGD directions) and diversity (minimizing RBF repulsion), solved via a fixed number of gradient descent steps with regularization parameter ν_t controlling the convergence-diversity trade-off.

modules.name: Adaptive Perturbation and Guidance Direction Assembly
modules.description: Implements the adaptive perturbation scaling mechanism (Eq. 14) that determines per-sample scaling factors γ_i^t based on the inner products between objective gradients and the perturbation direction, ensuring the combined guidance direction h̃_i^t = h_i^t + γ_i^t δ_t remains a common descent direction for all objectives.

modules.name: Armijo Backtracking Line Search
modules.description: Implements the Armijo condition-based backtracking line search to determine step sizes η_t at each reverse diffusion timestep, ensuring sufficient decrease in objective functions while preventing overly aggressive updates.

modules.name: Reverse Diffusion Sampling with Guided Updates
modules.description: Implements the full iterative reverse diffusion process (Eq. 9) starting from random noise, combining the DDPM denoising step with the MGD-guided and diversity-promoting update at each timestep, and applying crowding distance-based non-dominated point selection across successive timesteps to build the final approximate Pareto set.

modules.name: Crowding Distance Computation
modules.description: Implements the crowding distance metric for density estimation in objective space, computing per-objective normalized distances to immediate neighbors for non-dominated set sorting, with infinite distance assigned to boundary solutions to preserve Pareto front coverage during point selection.

modules.name: Offline MOO Adapter
modules.description: Adapts the SPREAD framework to the offline setting by replacing true objective evaluations with a pre-trained surrogate model F̃, using the offline dataset directly for DiT-MOO training, and applying the full guided sampling pipeline with surrogate-based gradient and objective computations.

modules.name: Bayesian MOO Adapter with SBX Escape
modules.description: Adapts SPREAD to multi-objective Bayesian optimization using iteratively updated Gaussian process surrogates, incorporating the simulated binary crossover (SBX) operator as an auxiliary escape mechanism for local optima, data augmentation strategies for training, and hypervolume-based batch selection within the iterative MOBO loop.

modules.name: Benchmark Problem Suite
modules.description: Implements the full suite of multi-objective optimization benchmark problems including synthetic test functions (ZDT1-3, ZDT4, ZDT6, DTLZ1-7) and real-world engineering design problems (RE21, RE22, RE25, RE31-37, RE41, RE42, RE61) with configurable input dimensions, numbers of objectives, and Pareto front shapes.

modules.name: Evaluation Metrics Computation
modules.description: Implements the three core evaluation metrics: hypervolume (HV) indicator measuring dominated objective-space volume relative to a reference point, Δ-spread measuring uniformity of solution distribution along the Pareto front, and log-hypervolume difference (LHD) for Bayesian optimization convergence tracking.

modules.name: Ablation Study and Scalability Analysis Framework
modules.description: Implements the systematic ablation framework covering diversity mechanism variants (without diversity, without repulsion, without perturbation), hyperparameter sensitivity studies (ν_t, ρ, number of DiT blocks L, number of main-direction optimization steps), transfer learning across related problems, scalability profiling (computational time vs. number of objectives, samples, and decision-space dimensionality), and result aggregation with automated table generation.
